study.question: Does signed oldest-to-newest target-match change add validation value beyond symmetric switching, unsigned change, latest state alone, and a capacity-matched duplicate readout?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: the incumbent switch-specific readout contains expected and observed undirected adjacency rates, which are exactly unchanged when timestamp-group probabilities are reversed. Its full model also contains recency and rank features, so full-model reversal invariance is NOT asserted. r0026-ordered_switch AUC0.6206353961 exceeds exchangeable0.6202195900 and duplicate0.6201337321 at seed42, but the gain over r0023-complement_newer_count0.6205084405 is small and selected. Hypothesis: signed target-match boundary drift distinguishes re-engagement from disengagement beyond the symmetric switch readout. This is a representation/conditional predictive hypothesis, not evidence of latent intent or causality. No new outcome has been measured.

nearest_work.difference: Inherits field-adapted attention; adds a deterministic per-field/action timestamp-boundary contrast to the existing local switch-statistic architecture. Original DIN uses unnormalized activation; our inherited softmax and blind query are local adaptations. DIN describes noisy sequential interests and a null LSTM experiment, not this signed endpoint statistic.

README verifies that histories lack item IDs; only category/brand/action/causal age are used. Publisher full text is blocked; neither a DMR reproduction nor a detailed architecture difference is asserted.

Retains all parent inputs, helpers, random draws and modules; exposes oldest/newest group match fractions from the same grouping and appends8 zero-initialized classifier columns. Reversal changes drift sign while preserving switch-specific features. Broad novelty remains unverified: registered searches for sequential/order, DIEN and DSIN returned no matches, not evidence of absence from literature.

inherited_components: Complete r0026-ordered_switch parent architecture/configuration, including all r0023 features, expected and observed switches, softmax history attention, embeddings and MLP
Existing positive-ID/action masks, exact-age tie grouping, causal supplied history128,3 epochs,batch4096,train seed42,first-six-day coverage,natural prevalence,Adam lr0.001 and fixed scorer
Original initialized parameter blocks and RNG consumption;8 appended deterministic zero columns shared across all4 variants
study.proposed_difference: Within each category/brand and action coordinate sort eligible events by increasing age and aggregate equal timestamps. For G>1 define newest=p[0], oldest=p[G-1], drift=newest-oldest, where p is the target-match fraction in a timestamp group. For G<=1 define every new readout0. Four otherwise identical cells append0.5 times drift, abs(drift), newest, or observed switch rate. Signed boundary direction is the sole candidate mechanism. All cells calculate every endpoint and switching statistic. Eight additional columns cost1024 parameters at hidden128; total predicted17141539. No optimizer/loss/input changes.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrast: signed_drift exceeds folded_drift in full-population validation ROC-AUC; signed direction has conditional utility beyond change magnitude. Record Logloss independently.
signed_drift should exceed duplicate_switch and the unchanged r0026-ordered_switch parent; beating only the unchanged parent is insufficient attribution.

signed_drift should exceed latest_endpoint if the older boundary contributes beyond latest target state. If it only ties latest_endpoint, interpret any gain as compatible with latest-state availability, not change detection.

Source/algebra checks: drift reverses sign under group reversal; abs(drift), expected and observed switches stay invariant; duplicate mode reproduces its existing switch coordinate exactly; G<=1/missing targets yield zero. Diagnostics report supported counts and positive/negative drift, without labels.

Exploratory frozen host slices: examine history_17_64 and history_gt64 separately; latter has3026583/3234051 impressions. Empty-history effects cannot directly demonstrate the endpoint mechanism. Report counts, no significance claims from one seed.
falsifiers: signed_drift does not beat folded_drift: this implementation offers no controlled support for directional value even if both beat duplicate.
signed_drift does not beat duplicate_switch or unchanged incumbent: no practical increment from endpoint direction under this recipe.
latest_endpoint matches or exceeds signed_drift: changes may reflect latest state rather than oldest-to-newest change.
Any nonzero endpoint readout for G<=1/missing target, bound violation, invalid input access, parent-prefix mismatch or nonfinite output invalidates that implementation.
Paired-seed reversals or small bootstrap intervals crossing zero weaken a seed42 improvement; no association is a causal mechanism proof.
alternative_explanations: Seed42 optimization variability and extensive validation selection across109 trajectories
Signed versus unsigned feature distributions affect optimization despite identical parameter count and initial predictions
Existing extrema, counts and decayed attention may already encode endpoint orientation; new readout may only ease optimization
Boundary effects from truncated128-event histories, coarse IDs, rare actions or unstable static snapshots
Latest target state alone, rather than a trend; additive columns and changed gradient geometry can improve any representation
Timestamp ties, lack of older full histories, and broad mixed user populations restrict interpretation; first512 diagnostics are not population evidence
